methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-institution cohort (25 patients, 22-month median follow-up). Univariate Cox proportional hazards analysis only; no multivariate modeling due to small sample size and limited events (20 recurrences). Appropriate Kaplan-Meier survival analysis but: severe sample size limitation (n=25); selection bias toward favorable disease biology and performance status; exploratory subgroup analyses without correction for multiple comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series of 25 patients with liver-only metastatic anal SCCA undergoing metastasectomy; real-world series with good outcomes (median OS 51.3 months) but lacks comparative control arm. Evidence level 4 (case series); findings descriptive rather than practice-changing given heterogeneity and selection bias inherent to metastasis-directed therapy populations.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows observational cohort structure with patient characteristics, treatment details, survival outcomes with Kaplan-Meier curves. Limitations section acknowledges retrospective design, selection bias, small sample size, limited power for multivariate analysis. However, no data availability statement; selection of highly favorable cohort (92% female, 80% single liver lesion, 80% with response to systemic therapy prior to surgery) limits generalizability.

novelty_literature.justification: Single-institution experience with liver metastasectomy for anal SCCA; adds to growing literature on metastasis-directed therapy. Median OS (51.3 months) exceeds InterAACT-2 data (~29 months at interim) but expected given extreme selection bias (only metastasis-directed therapy candidates with favorable biology). Incremental contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear Introduction establishing epidemiology and treatment rationale, detailed Methods describing cohort selection and outcomes assessment, Results presented with survival curves and univariate analysis, Discussion appropriately contextualizing findings against InterAACT and other literature. Limitations section thorough.

key_strengths: Addresses understudied topic: liver-directed therapy for rare disease (metastatic anal SCCA); median OS of 51.3 months substantially exceeds historical systemic therapy outcomes (~20-29 months)
Comprehensive patient selection with detailed documentation of baseline characteristics, systemic therapy response, surgical margins achieved (90% R0 resection)

Clear illustration of role for metastasis-directed therapy in favorable biology: all patients with preoperative chemotherapy had disease control prior to surgery; majority had metachronous rather than synchronous disease
Thoughtful Discussion contextualizing findings and acknowledging superior survival reflects careful patient selection rather than intervention efficacy
key_concerns: Extremely small sample size (n=25, 20 recurrences) prevents multivariate analysis and severely limits power to identify independent predictors; authors acknowledge but still attempt subgroup analyses
Severe selection bias: only patients with liver-only metastases, disease control on systemic therapy, and good performance status offered surgery; not representative of broader anal SCCA population
High recurrence rate (80%) with hepatic recurrence predominant questions durability of benefit; median DFS only 7.27 months despite OS of 51 months

No comparative control arm; lack of randomization or propensity matching limits causal inference; historical survival comparisons (InterAACT) may not be fully comparable due to patient and treatment differences
Cohort predominantly female (92%), HPV-positive (80%), immunocompetent—limiting generalizability to male, HPV-negative, HIV+ populations
chief_reviewer.rationale: Small single-institution case series demonstrating favorable OS outcomes with liver metastasectomy in highly selected anal SCCA patients. However, extreme selection bias, small sample size, and lack of comparative control preclude strong causal conclusions. Suitable for Tier 4 venue with major revisions: acknowledge selection bias limitations more prominently; prospective multicenter comparative trials needed to define true role of metastasis-directed therapy in modern treatment era.
